diagnostics.message: `module.runners:resource.aws_sqs_queue_policy.build_queue_dlq_policy` is created under the same condition as the dead-letter queue and is clearly intended to attach the deny-unsecure-transport policy to it, but `queue_url = aws_sqs_queue.queued_builds.id` points at the primary build queue instead. As a result the policy has no dependency on `module.runners:resource.aws_sqs_queue.queued_builds_dlq` and the DLQ is left without the TLS-enforcement policy (while the primary queue ends up with two `aws_sqs_queue_policy` resources fighting over the same `policy` attribute). Pointing `queue_url` at the DLQ both fixes the intent and establishes the ordering implicitly.

`module.webhook-github-app:resource.null_resource.update_app` calls the GitHub API (local-exec) to register the webhook URL passed in via `var.webhook_endpoint`, which resolves through `module.runners:output.webhook` = `aws_apigatewayv2_api.webhook.api_endpoint` + a hard-coded path string. That chain only orders the null_resource after the bare API Gateway API object — it does not depend on `module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_apigatewayv2_stage.webhook` (nor the integration/route), so the GitHub app can be pointed at `https://<api-id>.execute-api.<region>.amazonaws.com/webhook` before the `$default` stage is deployed and `POST /webhook` actually resolves. The webhook registration then fails/delivers 404s until the next apply. No clean attribute-level fix exists because the module only receives the endpoint as a plain string, so an explicit `depends_on` on the stage is the correct way to close the ordering gap.
